items.title: James Chirillo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Jerry Bruno... he played with Frank Sinatra... I called up Jerry Bruno... He introduced me to everybody he knew

ctx.x: Is there some, was there a big break for you when you look back on post-college then, was there a relationship with a particular musician or something that happened that you felt really opened things up?

There’s no one guy I can single out, I can name, for different aspects, of being able to stick around and stay alive. As a musician there’s plenty of guys I can name. I went to North Texas in spring, January, whatever, the spring semester but it starts in January of 1975. And I didn’t try out for a jazz band, they’d already pretty much had all that stuff settled from September or whatever, previous. But in the summer, for the summer bands, and I just stayed down there and went to school in the summer, for the…

had a great time. He said, “Man, if you ever come to New York give me a call.” So I ended up saving my money, I ended up joining the Army, in the band, I was in the band at West Point for three years, saved money, moved to New York in 1982, I called up Jerry Bruno and he said come down to the union on Wednesday, you’ll meet whatever, and I’ll introduce you to everybody I know. He introduced me to everybody he knew and a year later just about to the day I realized I had fifty dollars left in the bank. And no…
